### Frames

Now, along with `data` and `layout`, `frames` is added to the keys that `figure` allows. Your `frames` key points to a list of figures, each of which will be cycled through upon instantiation of the plot. With plotly.core, build the frames yourself (each frame holds the trace values to show at that step) and add a play button with `go_updatemenu()` or a slider with `go_slider()`.

### Cumulative Lines Animation

```{r}
library(plotly.core)
library(dplyr)

df <- ggplot2::txhousing |>
  filter(year > 2005, city %in% c("Abilene", "Bay Area"))
dates <- sort(unique(df$date))
cities <- unique(df$city)

# The data shown at each step: every row up to and including that date
accumulate_to <- function(d) {
  lapply(cities, function(cty) df[df$city == cty & df$date <= d, ])
}

fig <- go_figure()
first <- accumulate_to(dates[1])
for (k in seq_along(cities)) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(
      x = first[[k]]$date,
      y = first[[k]]$median,
      mode = "lines",
      name = cities[k]
    )
}

fig$frames <- lapply(dates, function(d) {
  list(
    name = as.character(d),
    data = lapply(accumulate_to(d), function(sub) {
      go_scatter(x = sub$date, y = sub$median)
    })
  )
})

fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(
    xaxis = go_xaxis(
      title = "Date",
      zeroline = FALSE,
      range = range(dates)
    ),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(
      title = "Median",
      zeroline = FALSE,
      range = range(df$median, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    updatemenus = list(
      go_updatemenu(
        type = "buttons",
        showactive = FALSE,
        x = 1,
        xanchor = "right",
        y = 0,
        yanchor = "bottom",
        buttons = list(
          go_updatemenu_button(
            label = "Play",
            method = "animate",
            args = list(
              NULL,
              list(
                frame = list(duration = 100, redraw = FALSE),
                transition = list(duration = 0),
                fromcurrent = TRUE,
                mode = "immediate"
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )

fig
```

### Filled-Area Animation

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
df <- tail(df, 30)
df$ID <- seq.int(nrow(df))

frame_trace <- function(sub) {
  go_scatter(
    x = sub$ID,
    y = sub$AAPL.Close,
    text = paste("Day: ", sub$ID, "<br>Close: $", sub$AAPL.Close)
  )
}

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    data = df[1, ],
    x = ~ID,
    y = ~AAPL.Close,
    mode = "lines",
    fill = "tozeroy",
    fillcolor = "rgba(114, 186, 59, 0.5)",
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "rgb(114, 186, 59)"),
    text = ~ paste("Day: ", ID, "<br>Close: $", AAPL.Close),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  )

fig$frames <- lapply(df$ID, function(id) {
  list(name = as.character(id), data = list(frame_trace(df[df$ID <= id, ])))
})

animate_args <- function(id) {
  list(
    list(as.character(id)),
    list(
      frame = list(duration = 100, redraw = FALSE),
      transition = list(duration = 0),
      mode = "immediate"
    )
  )
}

fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(
    title = "AAPL: Last 30 days",
    yaxis = go_yaxis(
      title = "Close",
      range = c(0, 250),
      zeroline = FALSE,
      tickprefix = "$"
    ),
    xaxis = go_xaxis(
      title = "Day",
      range = c(0, 30),
      zeroline = FALSE,
      showgrid = FALSE
    ),
    updatemenus = list(
      go_updatemenu(
        type = "buttons",
        showactive = FALSE,
        x = 0,
        xanchor = "right",
        y = 0,
        yanchor = "top",
        pad = go_updatemenu_pad(t = 60, r = 10),
        buttons = list(
          go_updatemenu_button(
            label = "Play",
            method = "animate",
            args = list(
              NULL,
              list(
                frame = list(duration = 100, redraw = FALSE),
                transition = list(duration = 0),
                fromcurrent = TRUE,
                mode = "immediate"
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    ),
    sliders = list(
      go_slider(
        currentvalue = go_slider_currentvalue(prefix = "Day "),
        pad = go_slider_pad(t = 50),
        steps = lapply(df$ID, function(id) {
          go_slider_step(
            label = as.character(id),
            method = "animate",
            args = animate_args(id)
          )
        })
      )
    )
  )

fig
```
